blocks.sourceSectionTitle: What qualifications actually matter for entry-level business analyst roles

rows: Commerce, business administration, economics, and MBA graduates move in fastest, especially at consulting firms, banks, and large enterprises that recruit BAs directly from campus. But this is not a closed field, engineering graduates who prefer stakeholder-facing work over pure coding, and even science or arts graduates with strong communication and structured thinking, get hired regularly, especially in IT services.

No. Job postings for entry-level BA roles routinely accept "any graduate" alongside preferred fields. What most postings actually entry requirement on is analytical thinking, MS Excel skill, communication skill, and some exposure to how a business process works, not the exact degree name on your certificate.

Yes, meaningfully, for speed of entry at consulting firms and larger enterprises that run campus BA hiring. But an MBA is not a requirement for every entry point, plenty of BAs enter through IT services or a junior operations role first and build the title over 1-2 years without ever doing an MBA.

Employers now expect basic SQL, a documentation tool (Jira, Confluence), and comfort with a process-mapping tool (Visio or Lucidchart) even at entry level. You do not need to code, but "I only know Excel" is a weaker application than it was five years ago.
